items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: Joe Farrell — Monk, you know his name I know, Joe Farrell who played with Corea and had a good career as a solo saxophone player. He was a flute major at Illinois.

ctx.x: It’s rather stunning, the state of jazz education how it just sort of exploded over the years and now it’s an integral part of almost any music school across the country.

Yeah, it is. And also, the saxophone. I’ll tell you, in the 1960s there were not many places you could study saxophone and get a degree. Joe Farrell — Monk, you know his name I know, Joe Farrell who played with Corea and had a good career as a solo saxophone © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
player. He was a flute major at Illinois. They didn’t have saxophone. He couldn’t major in saxophone, it was in flute.
